title: Concurrent Multi-Query Acquisition Coherence: Naive vs Version-Fenced Double-Collect
motivation: Proposition 1's coherence assumption (A4) requires commit-time observations to correspond to one coherent acquisition state, or equivalently that relevant state remains stable during acquisition. The manuscript discloses that the prototype does not implement a general cross-resource snapshot protocol. This experiment implements and empirically tests one concrete mechanism -- version-fenced double-collect with bounded retry -- against genuine concurrent mutation of the same three physical resources DCJI selects in the F5 multi-basis scenario (obs-a, obs-c, obs-e), and measures whether it actually prevents delivering an incoherent (torn) multi-query view, compared to a naive sequential multi-query acquisition with no coherence check.

mutator.description: A background thread continuously toggles a uniformly-random one of the three resources' valid field between true/false, as fast as HTTP PATCH round-trips allow, for the duration of each trial window. Every toggle is logged with wall-clock timestamp, resource, new value, and new resourceVersion, providing ground truth against which acquired views are checked for coherence.

coherence_definition: An acquired combination of (resource, value) pairs is COHERENT if and only if there exists at least one instant t during the trial at which every queried resource's ground-truth value (reconstructed from the mutator's timestamped toggle log plus the trial's known initial state) equals the value returned to that acquisition for that resource. It is INCOHERENT otherwise -- i.e., the returned combination never existed as a single real simultaneous state.
notes: Preregistered post-hoc extension (E24), run outside the locked v8.1.1 package and outside all other v9/E21/E23 evidence. Uses a dedicated namespace/ConfigMaps, not E21's, to avoid touching already-finalized E21 evidence.
